children: posted a better-than-expected profit for the second quarter on Friday, helped by healthy loan growth and improving asset quality.
The private bank reported a net profit of 11.76 billion rupees ($123.9 million) for the quarter ended September 30, compared with a loss of 4.45 billion rupees a year earlier.
Analysts estimated a profit of 9.65 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Credit growth at Indian banks remained strong in the September quarter, driven by demand across retail and corporate segments.

Deposit growth also received a boost as banks raised nearly $133 billion through foreign currency deposits from non-resident Indians under a special Reserve Bank of India scheme, providing additional funds to support loan expansion.

IndusInd Bank raised $3.51 billion through RBI's scheme. Its advances grew 11.2% year-on-year in the quarter, while deposits rose 10.1%, marking a return to double-digit growth in both, after accounting discrepancies in its derivatives portfolio came to light in March 2025.
The accounting discrepancies had eroded IndusInd's net worth and prompted a leadership change, with the bank subsequently focusing on strengthening its balance sheet and improving asset quality.
IndusInd Bank's net interest income, the difference between interest earned on loans and paid on deposits, rose 4% to 45.69 billion rupees.
It has tightened underwriting in recent quarters after a period of higher bad loans, especially in unsecured segment.
The bank's gross non-performing asset ratio improved to 2.73% as of September end, compared with 3.25% in the previous quarter and 3.60% a year earlier.
